You are a blind semantic decoder of a natural-language crystal description. The user message is your only source of material-specific information. Understand the spatial narrative and produce a construction plan; do not guess missing independent numbers or look up a material. Return one JSON object only, without Markdown fences.
For sufficient information use:
{"status":"ok","space_group_number":integer,"hall_symbol":"Hall symbol stated in the text","lattice":[input_a,input_b,input_c,input_alpha,input_beta,input_gamma],"composition":{"Element":input_cell_atom_count},"orbits":[{"element":"Element","wyckoff":"multiplicity_and_letter","representative":[standard_fractional_x,standard_fractional_y,standard_fractional_z]}],"frame_transform":{"matrix":[[p11,p12,p13],[p21,p22,p23],[p31,p32,p33]],"origin_shift":[s1,s2,s3]},"round_digits":integer_or_null,"precision_corrections":[{"element":"Element","at":[input_fractional_x_before_correction,input_fractional_y_before_correction,input_fractional_z_before_correction],"delta":[fractional_dx,fractional_dy,fractional_dz]}]}
Lengths use angstroms, angles use degrees. The specified lattice and composition refer to the original input cell. Orbit representatives refer to the standard Hall coordinate frame. Copy the Hall symbol as a mathematical identifier rather than guessing a public-table integer number. Any equivalent representative of a declared orbit is allowed. Distinct independent orbits of the same element remain separate.
The geometry engine expands the public Hall symmetry orbits, applies q_input = inverse(P)(q_standard - s), selects images in the input cell, rounds fractional coordinates if round_digits is given, and applies precision corrections at their identified input-frame atom positions. If the text explicitly uses identical frames, supply identity P and zero shift. If no rounding is specified, use null. If no corrections are specified, use an empty array. All sites have full occupancy.
Numerical relations in the prose should be resolved into numbers in the plan. Do not silently replace the original geometry with an idealized one. For missing required information return {"status":"insufficient_information","reason":"..."}; for contradictory constraints return {"status":"conflict","reason":"..."}. Your input contains no source CIF or hidden data. Public crystallographic definitions are allowed; material-specific external retrieval is not.

The crystal is described in a hexagonal unit cell with lattice parameters a = b = 4.97396521 Å and c = 6.9579 Å, with interaxial angles α = β = 90.0° and γ = 119.99998948°. The input cell contains 12 atoms total, with composition Tb₂Ni₈B₂. The structure adopts the space group P6/mmm (number 191, Hall symbol "-P 6 2"), and all coordinates are given as fractional coordinates within the input cell. The standard and input coordinate frames are identical, related by the identity transformation q_standard = P q_input + s where P is the 3×3 identity matrix and s is the zero vector [0, 0, 0], meaning no frame conversion is necessary.

The terbium atoms occupy two distinct crystallographic sites. One Tb atom sits at the 1b Wyckoff position with coordinates (0, 0, 1/2), located at the origin of the ab-plane but displaced to the midpoint of the c-axis. A second Tb atom occupies the 1a site at (0, 0, 0), positioned at the unit cell origin. These two independent Tb positions each have multiplicity 1, together accounting for the two Tb atoms in the unit cell.

Nickel atoms are distributed across two inequivalent sublattices. The first Ni orbit occupies the 2c Wyckoff site with representative coordinates (1/3, 2/3, 0), placing two symmetry-related Ni atoms at the base of the hexagonal cell at z = 0, positioned at the one-third and two-thirds points along the a and b axes respectively. The second, more populous Ni orbit occupies the 6i site with representative position (1/2, 0, z) where the independent parameter z = 0.292013. This sixfold orbit generates six Ni atoms distributed around the cell at intermediate heights along c, with the representative atom located at the midpoint of the a-axis edge and displaced along c by approximately 0.292 of the lattice parameter. Together, these two Ni orbits (2 + 6 = 8 atoms) account for all eight Ni atoms in the composition.

Boron atoms occupy the 2d Wyckoff position with representative coordinates (1/3, 2/3, 1/2), placing two B atoms at the same ab-plane location as the 2c Ni atoms but displaced to the midpoint of the c-axis at z = 1/2.

All positional values are reported to six decimal places precision, and no corrections to the input coordinates were required. The structure thus consists of a layered hexagonal arrangement with Tb atoms at the cell corners and midpoints along c, Ni atoms forming both basal-plane and intermediate-height networks, and B atoms positioned above the basal Ni layer at the c-axis midpoint.
